transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... it's probably just a little misunderstanding at work, really. I just want to do a good job, you know? 

I'm a personal care aide, and we had this staff meeting recently. I guess I just got a little too worked up about safety protocols. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill for everybody. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms to show them exactly how to catch someone, just trying to be helpful. But, um... I guess I couldn't seem to stop doing it, even when folks told me to sit down. I just got really carried away. It was a bit embarrassing, honestly, but I'm totally fine now. 

Is it okay that I'm starting with that? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Has something like that happened to you before?

Um, no, I don't really think so. I mean... maybe I've gotten a little excited about things before, but nothing like that where I couldn't seem to stop, you know? 

I usually just try to be a really good employee and do exactly what I'm told. I definitely don't want you to think I'm a troublemaker or disruptive or anything like that. It was really just an isolated thing... just me trying a little too hard to help out the team. I haven't had any other complaints from my supervisor before this. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Did this incident at work cause you any problems with your relationships with your coworkers or supervisor?

Um, well... I guess my supervisor thought it would be best if I took a little breather. So, they did put me on leave from the senior center. Just for now, you know, to rest up and get my bearings. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but... I guess I haven't really been keeping up with things at home the way I usually do, either. My wife has had to remind me about my chores and some appointments I had. I really try to be a good husband and stay on top of things, I promise, it's just been a little harder lately. 

I've also kind of pulled back from my friends at church. Just staying quiet, mostly. I guess I've just been worrying a lot about whether I can safely go back to my caregiving work. I love my job and I don't want to let anyone down. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad worker or anything... I'm really trying my best to get back on track. Did I explain that okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people can't?

Um... gosh. I really don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I definitely don't see things, I promise. But... well, I guess maybe just a little bit with the hearing part? 

Sometimes when I'm all by myself in the hallway at the center, or... or even just at home down by the laundry room, I'll hear my name. Or it sounds exactly like one of the residents calling out for help, just clear as day. I always go check right away, because I want to make sure everyone is safe, but... there isn't anybody there when I look. 

I figure it's just because I'm so dedicated to my job, you know? Like my ears are just playing tricks on me because I'm always on high alert, listening out for the folks who might need me. It doesn't mean I'm crazy or anything. That doesn't make me sound too weird, does it? I just want to be totally honest with you, but I hope that's a normal thing when you're just trying really hard to be a good caregiver.
Are you still hearing your name or the residents calling out for help when you're alone?

Um... yes, I am. I really hope that doesn't mean I'm getting worse, I promise I try my best to just ignore it when it happens. If I'm being completely honest—and I really want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions—it's actually been going on for a little while now. 

I'd say... maybe about nine months or so? The hearing the calls that aren't there, and... well, I guess also having some suspicious thoughts, too. Just kind of worrying and wondering about things a bit too much. I know nine months probably sounds like a long time, and I'm really sorry I didn't mention it sooner. I just didn't want you to think I was, you know, totally losing my grip or being a bad patient. 

It's just my mind playing tricks because I want to be a good caregiver, right? I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this now... did I answer that the right way for you?
Do you find it hard to organize your thoughts or express them clearly to others?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope not. I try really hard to make sure I'm being clear when I talk to people. 

I guess sometimes my mind gets a little busy, you know, with wanting to make sure I'm doing a good job and all... but I don't think my thoughts are disorganized or anything like that. I can usually get my point across okay. At least, I hope I do. 

Have I been making sense to you today? I really want to make sure I'm answering everything the way you need me to. I'm trying my best to be clear, I promise.
Do you believe there's any truth to the voices you're hearing or the thoughts that someone might be calling for help when no one is there?

Um... well, with the voices, I really do think it's just my ears playing tricks on me, like I said. But... gosh, I hope this doesn't sound too strange, and I'm really not trying to sound paranoid or anything... 

But with the thoughts... even when I'm having a good day and feeling totally calm, I do kind of believe that... well, that my supervisor and a couple of the other people at work are... sort of keeping notes on me? Like they're watching me extra close and testing me with these little comments they make. 

I just get this really strong feeling that they're trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors. Which isn't true at all, I promise! I would never hurt anyone, I care about them so much. I just... I don't know why I feel so sure they're doing that. 

I know it probably sounds a little crazy, and I'm sorry if it does. I really try not to let it bother me at work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too difficult or anything, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole truth.
Have you been having trouble completing your daily tasks or have you noticed any changes in your behavior that are out of the ordinary for you?

Um... well... I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or anything. I really do try to keep up with things. But... my wife, she's been a little frustrated with me lately. 

She says I've just been sitting in the living room a lot, staring at the TV with the volume turned way down. And... I guess I haven't been calling my friends from church like I usually do, either. 

I know the chores around the house need doing, and I really want to do them, I promise. It's just... I don't know, it feels harder lately to just get up and start them. I know I should be doing better, and I'm really sorry if that makes me sound like a bad husband or a bad patient. I'm trying, I really am. 

Is it okay that I'm struggling with that a little bit right now? I hope I'm not disappointing you.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping from one idea to another without any connection?

Um... well, sometimes, maybe a little bit? I hope that doesn't make me sound scattered or... like I'm not paying attention. I really do try my best to stay focused on what I'm doing. 

But... yeah, I guess sometimes my mind just goes really fast. It'll jump from thinking about my job, and then suddenly I'm thinking about church, and then my wife, and then... like, all these new workshop ideas I want to do. It just bounces around so fast that... well, sometimes I lose the very first thought before I can even say it right out loud. 

I'm really sorry if that makes me hard to talk to today. I'm trying so hard to keep everything straight for you so I can give you good answers. Does that make sense? I just hope I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
Do you often find yourself having trouble finding the right words when trying to express your thoughts?

Um... no, I don't think I have that problem. I hope that's okay to say? I usually know exactly what words I want to use. It's just... well, like I mentioned before, sometimes there are just so many thoughts happening at once. But when I do catch one of those thoughts, I know how to say it. 

I really try my best to be clear when I talk, especially with the folks I care for at work. I wouldn't want to confuse them. Am I making sense to you today? I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers and not being difficult to understand.
Do you think that things you see or hear on TV, or read in the newspaper, are specifically about you or related to you in some way?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I know some people get really caught up in the news and think it's all about them, but I try really hard to just watch the TV for what it is. 

I know the news is just for everybody, you know? I wouldn't want to seem full of myself or anything, thinking the reporters were talking to me specifically. I just... I just watch it quietly. Like my wife said, with the volume down. 

Is it good that I don't feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything else that might be... well, out of the ordinary, like you said before. I really am trying to be a good patient.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other?

Um... no, not really. I hope that's what you're looking for? I mean, like I was saying before, they can go pretty fast sometimes, but they still... they still make sense to me. They connect, just maybe a little quicker than usual. 

I try really hard to keep my thoughts organized, especially for my job. I wouldn't want to seem like my mind is just... falling apart or anything. I'm doing my best to keep everything straight. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
Do you feel like you can stop thinking about something when you want to?

Um... yes, I believe so. If I need to stop thinking about a certain thing, I just... I just push it out of my mind. Is that what you mean? 

Like, if I'm helping one of my guys at work, I can't be distracted, so I just tell myself to focus on them instead. And it works. I don't really get stuck on things. I hope it's a good sign that I can do that? I really try my best to stay on track and be reliable. 

You don't think it's a bad thing to just... move on from a thought like that, do you? I just want to make sure I'm doing okay and giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think that there are people talking about you or plotting against you when you're not around?

Um... well, no, not like plotting against me. I know that sounds crazy, and I'm definitely not crazy. I just... I do worry sometimes about work, but I think that's normal, right? 

I work as an aide with seniors, and it's a big responsibility. So, even when my mood is totally fine and I'm calm, I... well, I do get this feeling that my supervisor and a couple of the other aides are... keeping tabs on me. Like they're taking notes on what I do. 

Sometimes they make these little comments, and it feels like a test. Like they're trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the seniors or something. But I'm very careful, I promise. I do a good job. Is it okay that I feel that way? I mean, it's just me wanting to be sure I'm doing things right, you know? It doesn't mean I'm paranoid or anything bad like that, does it?
Do you think that people are talking about you or watching you for a specific reason when you're out in public?

Um... no, not really. I don't think strangers are watching me or anything like that. That would be a bit strange, wouldn't it? 

I just go about my business when I'm out. You know, going to the store, running errands... I just blend in. I don't feel like anyone is paying special attention to me. I try to be polite and keep to myself, so there's no reason for anyone to be talking about me anyway. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, it shows I'm grounded in reality and everything. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I don't have those kinds of thoughts about people in public. Is that what you were hoping to hear?
Do you think that certain events or things that happen around you are specifically related to you or have a special meaning for you?

Um... no, no, I don't think so. Like, if I see something on the news or... or hear a song on the radio, it's just a song, you know? It's for everyone. 

I don't think the universe is sending me secret messages or anything like that. I know that would be... well, that wouldn't be very healthy, right? I just try to take things at face value. If something happens, it's just a coincidence. 

I'm pretty practical like that. I think you have to be in my line of work. You just focus on what's right in front of you. That's the normal way to look at things, isn't it? I really try to just be sensible about all that.
Do you often find yourself having difficulty sticking to one topic when talking to others?

Well, um... I guess sometimes I might get a little ahead of myself when I'm talking. But it's just because I have a lot of good things going on, you know? 

Like, my mind will jump from my job with the seniors, and then to church, and then to my wife, and then I get these really great ideas for a new workshop... and it just goes so fast. Sometimes I lose the first thought before I can even say it right. 

But that just means I'm enthusiastic, right? It's not like I can't hold a conversation. I just have a lot of passion for the things in my life. People like it when you have a lot to say, don't they? I try really hard to be a good conversationalist. Is it okay that my mind works a little fast sometimes?
Do you often have thoughts that don't make sense to you or seem unrelated to what's happening around you?

Well, no, not really. I mean, my thoughts are pretty normal, I think. I don't sit around having weird, random thoughts that don't make any sense. 

I try to stay focused on what I'm doing, like taking care of my clients or helping out at church. My thoughts are usually just about practical things, you know? What's for dinner, or what time I need to be at work. 

I guess everyone has a random thought pop into their head every now and then, but nothing that doesn't make sense to me. I like to keep things organized in my head. That's a good way to be, right? It means I'm staying grounded. I really try to make sure my thoughts are always appropriate for whatever situation I'm in. Does that sound like a healthy way to think?
Do you find it hard to stick to one topic when talking to others and then come back to it later?

Um, no, not really. I think... well, I mean, I know we just talked about how my mind goes a little fast sometimes, but I don't think I lose track of things completely. 

If I'm talking to someone, I can always bring it back around. I'm pretty good at that. Like, if I get excited about a new idea for church, I might talk about that for a minute, but I always remember to ask the other person how they're doing or finish the story I started first. 

I don't just wander off and leave people confused. That would be rude, wouldn't it? I always try to be polite and make sure the other person is following along. It's important to be a good listener too, right? I really try to make sure I'm doing both when I have a conversation.
Do you think that certain things that happen to you or around you have a special meaning that's just for you?

Well, um... I wouldn't say "special meaning," exactly. That makes it sound a little strange, doesn't it? I just... I try to be really observant, especially at work. 

I mean, I love my job working with the seniors, and I want to do a good job. But sometimes... even when I'm feeling totally calm and fine, I just kind of notice things. Like, I get this feeling that my supervisor and a couple of the others are... well, maybe keeping notes on me? 

It's just little things they say, you know? Little comments here and there. It feels like they're testing me, maybe trying to prove I'm not safe to be around the clients. But I am safe! I'm very careful. I just... I pick up on those little hints they drop. 

It's normal to be aware of your surroundings at work, right? It just means I'm paying attention to my performance. I really want them to see that I'm doing a good job. Is it okay that I notice those kinds of things?
